name: Studio
purpose: A design studio that lives in your repo: studies, engineering notes, and working UI experiments kept beside the code they describe, open to the agents that help you build it.

items.title: Agent dispatch
items.summary: studio/agents lets a Studio register the agents it may send work to and route messages — annotations, context, review passes — to a chosen agent over the existing Scout web transport. items.title: Share studies as Claude artifacts
items.summary: A study is easy to review in Studio itself, if the reviewer has the repo running. Most reviewers don't. Studio can bundle any study into one self-contained page and publish it as a Claude artifact: a private link you can share like a document. Comments left on the artifact come back into Studio as feedback on the study

items.title: Cloud deploy
items.summary: Shipping design studios to a VM's multi-studio host? See docs/cloud-studios.md — this document covers the platform app deploy (studio.service, releases under /studio-cloud/<release-id>).

items.title: Cloud studios — one host, many studios, git-push sync
items.summary: A VM runs one Vite host process that serves every studio from real source. Studios are small private git repos; git push ships them, the cloud coding agent edits them in place, and locals pull its commits back. No built assets cross the wire in either direction — only source, transformed per request.

items.title: Component registry
items.summary: @arach/studio/components is the component-level sibling of the page registry (@arach/studio/registry). The page registry describes the routes a studio hosts; the component registry describes the components it has finished, so a human or an agent can tell an adoptable component from a sketch without reading its source.

items.title: Studio reference
items.summary: Studio gives product teams a place to keep design studies, engineering notes, and working UI experiments beside the code they describe.
